root_cause.text: The `stm32_usbphyc_probe` function performs an incorrect bounds check on the device tree-provided `index` variable by using the `>` operator instead of `>=`, which allows an out-of-bounds access to the `usbphyc->phys[]` array when `index` is equal to `usbphyc->nphys`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the validation condition in `drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c` being corrected from `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)` to `if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys)`. Additionally, the commit message states that "index" is used as an index into the `usbphyc->phys[]` array (which has `usbphyc->nphys` elements), meaning an index equal to `usbphyc->nphys` is one element out of bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in stm32_usbphyc_probe to prevent out-of-bounds indexing.
intent_record.what: The comparison operator in the boundary check for 'index' was changed from greater-than (>) to greater-than-or-equal-to (>=) relative to 'usbphyc->nphys'.
intent_record.how: This change prevents an off-by-one error by ensuring that 'index', which is used for zero-based indexing, cannot be equal to the total number of PHYs ('nphys'), thereby avoiding potential out-of-bounds access.

    phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)
    
    This patch adds phy transceiver driver for STM32 USB PHY Controller
    (USBPHYC) that provides dual port High-Speed phy for OTG (single port)
    and EHCI/OHCI host controller (two ports).
    One port of the phy is shared between the two USB controllers through
    a UTMI+ switch.
